teach_en: ກ is a consonant. At the start of a syllable it is an unaspirated k, said with no puff of air, so English ears often hear a g (as in 'gas').
notes: From letters.csv C01 pron_tip (verified); wording by agent.

teach_en: A short 'ee', tighter than the i in 'bin'. Written above the consonant, but said after it. A vowel is one unit, wherever its parts sit, and the consonant it goes with is always said first.
notes: From vowels.csv V04 pron_tip (verified); wording by agent.

teach_en: ນ at the end of a syllable is n, as in 'sun'. (At the start of a syllable it is also n, as in 'no'.)
notes: From letters.csv C13 (ipa_final n; verified); wording by agent.
